children: India’s largest private-sector lender reports a year-on-year increase in second-quarter profit, while net interest income falls short of forecasts and provisions rise amid improving asset quality

HDFC Bank reported a 4.7 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 19,510 crore for the second quarter of the 2026–27 financial year, but the result fell short of market expectations.
The lender’s net profit was below the Bloomberg estimate of Rs 19,727 crore. It had reported a profit of Rs 18,641 crore in the corresponding quarter a year earlier.
The results, announced on Saturday, 17 October, reflect continued growth in the bank’s core lending business, alongside higher provisioning expenses and weaker-than-expected operating performance.
Net Interest Income Misses Forecast
Net interest income (NII), which measures the difference between interest earned on loans and interest paid on deposits, rose 10 per cent year-on-year to Rs 34,619 crore.
However, the figure was below the estimated Rs 34,991 crore.
Operating profit increased 5.6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 29,483 crore, compared with Rs 27,923 crore in the year-ago period. The result also missed the market estimate of Rs 29,868 crore.
The bank’s net interest margin (NIM), based on total assets, stood at 3.16 per cent.
Provisions Increase, Asset Quality Improves
HDFC Bank’s provisions rose to Rs 3,574 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 3,059 crore in the preceding quarter and Rs 3,500 crore a year earlier.
Despite the increase in provisions, asset quality improved sequentially.

The gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio declined to 1.11 per cent from 1.17 per cent in the previous quarter, beating the estimated 1.14 per cent. The net NPA ratio also fell to 0.37 per cent from 0.41 per cent, against an estimate of 0.39 per cent.
The improvement in these ratios indicates a lower proportion of stressed loans relative to the bank’s advances, although provisioning costs remain an important factor for earnings.
Loan Growth Remains Strong
HDFC Bank continued to expand its lending portfolio during the quarter.

Average advances under management increased 14.1 per cent year-on-year to Rs 31.87 lakh crore. Gross advances at the end of September stood at Rs 32.20 lakh crore, representing growth of 16.3 per cent from a year earlier.
Retail loans grew 11.7 per cent year-on-year, while lending to small and mid-market enterprises increased 23.5 per cent.

On the funding side, average deposits rose 16.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 31.66 lakh crore. Average current account and savings account (CASA) deposits increased 10.7 per cent to Rs 9.71 lakh crore.
The results highlight the bank’s continued loan and deposit growth, even as its profitability metrics remain below market expectations in some key areas.
